source_text: Ἰγνάτιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, Πολυκάρπῳ ἐπισκόπῳ ἐκκλησίας Σμυρναίων, μᾶλλον ἐπισκοπημένῳ ὑπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, πλεῖστα χαίρειν.
thought_title: Greeting to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to Polycarp, bishop of the church in Smyrna, with a formal greeting.
pass_a_gloss: Ignatius, the [one] also [called] God-Bearer, to Polycarp bishop of [the] church of Smyrna, rather [one] watched over by God [the] Father and [the] Lord Jesus Christ, very many [greetings].

choices.why: The epithet means 'bearing God' and is rendered literally to preserve the title's force.
The passive participle of ἐπισκοπέω is distinct from the noun ἐπίσκοπος; rendering it as 'watched over' preserves the wordplay and the passive sense.
The standard epistolary formula is rendered literally to keep the formal greeting register.
The adverb marks a correction or refinement of the preceding title, so 'rather' preserves that nuance.

pass_b_english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, sends very many greetings to Polycarp, bishop of the church of Smyrna, or rather to one who is watched over by God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'bishop' for ἐπίσκοπος derivatives; 'watched over' avoids the term.
last_rejected.fix: one who is bishoped by God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπισκοπημένῳ is a verb participle, not ἐπίσκοπος; 'watched over' fits the passive 'overseen' and breaks no glossary.

last_rejected.why: ἐπισκοπημένῳ is passive of ἐπισκοπέω, 'to oversee/bishop,' not generic 'watch over.'
last_rejected.fix: one who is bishoped by God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπισκοπέω includes 'look upon, care for'; passive 'watched over' is within normal range, not a mistranslation.

problems.why: Title for Ignatius vs. description of Ephesians; reader may conflate the two uses.
problems.fix: Capitalize 'God-Bearer' as Ignatius's title; lowercase the plural for the Ephesians.
